findings.note: Wrong case and agreement: the object should be accusative ("určuje farbu") and "zrakovej vnímania" mixes feminine genitive with a neuter noun, producing a nonsensical phrase (natural: "určuje farbu, ktorú vnímame zrakom"); the question is still answerable but sounds broken when read aloud.
"soustavy" is the Czech form; Slovak requires "sústavy" — a Czech word inside Slovak output that a native speaker would immediately correct (occurs in both the question and the explanation).

The film title "Sinners" is rendered as the non-existent word "Grešníci" (Slovak for sinners is "hriešnici", and the film's Slovak release title is "Hriešnici"), so a player who says the real title — original or Slovak — is graded wrong.
The explanation repeats the invented title, so it no longer supports a recognisable correct answer.

"Ginger cat" is calqued literally as "zázvorová mačka" (zázvor = the spice ginger); Slovak uses "ryšavá"/"oranžová" (or "zrzavá") for this coat colour, so the phrase is nonsense to a native listener and clashes with "oranžovú srsť" in the same item's explanation.
The option values are ordinary words left in English while the stem asks "Pravda alebo nepravda", so a Slovak player who says "pravda" is not matching any option and cannot answer the item in Slovak.
The correct answer is left in English, so the spoken Slovak answer "pravda" will be graded as wrong.

The cardinal numeral "sedem" is rendered as the ordinal "siedme" ("seventh") and the phrase is not properly declined; a native would say "všetkých ostatných sedem planét", and the read-aloud question sounds ungrammatical, though the item is still answerable.
The correct answer key moved from a to b and the answer changed from the Danube to the Vltava, so a Slovak player who correctly says "Dunaj" is graded wrong.

findings.span: Vltava preteká Bratislavou na ceste z Viedne do Budapešti.
findings.note: The explanation now asserts the Vltava flows through Bratislava, which is false and reinforces the flipped answer instead of supporting the source answer (the Danube).

The question was replaced by the two-word fragment "suchy bodliak" (also missing the diacritic in "suchý"), so nothing of the source question survives and the item is unplayable — the player hears no question to answer.
The fragment served as the question names the plant itself, handing the player the answer instead of asking for it.

The primary correct answer is left in English although Slovak has the established term "stepný bežec" (used here only as an alternative), so the reference answer is not in the language the player is speaking.

The explanation drops the source's key qualifier that this is an English collective noun, so in Slovak it asserts the false claim that a group of crows is called 'vražda' and leaves the player with no idea why the answer is right.
Word-for-word rendering of the colloquial 'hanging out together'; 'zdržujú sa' is stiff and unidiomatic when spoken aloud, though the question is still understandable and gradable.
Direct calque of English 'What do you call'; natural spoken Slovak would use the impersonal 'Ako sa nazýva', but nothing is broken.
The correct answer "Gold" was rendered as "Striebro" (silver), so a Slovak player who correctly says "Zlato" is graded wrong.

findings.span: Značka Au pochádza z latinského argentum.
findings.note: The explanation replaces Latin "aurum" with "argentum" and drops the gloss "meaning gold", cementing the wrong answer and teaching the player a false fact.

findings.span: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
findings.note: The question is left entirely in English, so a Slovak player hearing it read aloud cannot understand or answer the item in Slovak.

The source unit "kilometres" was changed to miles, so the Slovak correct answer states a completely different depth (11 miles ≈ 17.7 km) and a player answering correctly in kilometres is graded wrong.

findings.span: Challenger Deep siaha približne 10,9 míle pod hladinu mora.
findings.note: The explanation likewise converts 10.9 kilometres to miles, contradicting the real figure and no longer supporting the source answer.
The Slovak name of the feature is "Mariánska priekopa" (feminine); the invented masculine form with wrong agreement is what a native speaker would correct.
Slovak has the established form "Challengerova hlbočina"; leaving the English name untouched is a lazy half-translation, though the item stays playable.
The Slovak title of The Godfather is 'Krstný otec'; 'Krstný syn' means 'godson', so a player who correctly says 'Krstný otec' is graded wrong.

findings.span: Repliku vyslovuje Vito Corleone vo filme Krstný syn.
findings.note: The explanation repeats the wrong film title, so it no longer supports the correct answer and reinforces the mis-grading.

"Rotovať" mirrors English "rotate"; a native would more naturally say "prehadzovať pneumatiky" (the noun "rotácia pneumatík" is common, the verb less so) — the item remains fully playable and gradable.

findings.span: Prečo cibule robia teba plakať, keď ich sekáš?
findings.note: "robia teba plakať" is a word-for-word calque of "make you cry" (and uses the stressed pronoun "teba" instead of the clitic "ťa"); natural Slovak would be "Prečo nám pri krájaní cibule slzia oči?".
"sekať" (to hack/chop with a blade) is not the normal Slovak verb for cutting up an onion — "krájaš" is, and the explanation itself already uses "Krájanie".
Redundant English-style subject pronoun, and the wrong gender form at that (cibuľa is feminine, so "ony/one"); Slovak would simply drop it: "Uvoľňujú...".

Literal rendering of "irritates the eyes" via a light verb; Slovak says "dráždi oči", and the odd phrasing appears in both the correct answer and the alternative answer, so a player who says the natural "dráždi oči" may be graded against an unnatural key.

findings.span: robí reakciu s vlhkosťou v oku
findings.note: "reacts with" calqued as "robí reakciu s"; correct Slovak is "reaguje s vlhkosťou v oku".

The German name Joachimsthal was replaced by the Czech/Slovak name Jáchymov, which is the correct answer, so the question now states the answer outright (and is also factually false, since Jáchymov is not the German form).
The non-inflecting band name "Queen" is declined into a possessive adjective "Queenina", a form a native speaker would correct to "štvrtý štúdiový album skupiny Queen".
The song title "Imagine" must stay in its original form; a Slovak player will say "Imagine" aloud and be graded wrong against the invented Slovak title.

Slovak has the established form "vombat" (Vombat obyčajný); the English spelling is kept in both the answer and the explanation ("wombata"), which a native speaker would correct, though the spoken answer still matches phonetically.
The song title "Bohemian Rhapsody" — which is the correct answer — was literally translated; a player who says the real title aloud will not match the Slovak answer string and will be graded wrong.
The correct answer field invents a Slovak title that no release uses, so the spoken original "Bohemian Rhapsody" no longer denotes the same string being graded against.

findings.span: b) Rozhýbeme ťa | c) Niekoho na milovanie
findings.note: Distractor song titles "We Will Rock You" and "Somebody to Love" were translated into invented Slovak phrases, so the option set no longer matches the source and the distractors are unrecognisable as Queen songs.

findings.span: Bohémska rapsódia bola na vrchole britského rebríčka
findings.note: The explanation repeats the invented title instead of the original, so it no longer supports the answer the player would actually say.
Slovak has the established form "toliar" for this coin; a player will say "toliar" aloud and be graded wrong against the German/English form "Thaler", making the item effectively ungradable.

findings.span: Názov joachimsthaler sa skrátil na thaler, z ktorého angličtina prevzala slovo dolár.
findings.note: The explanation keeps "thaler" instead of the Slovak "toliar" (from "jáchymovský toliar"), so it does not support the answer a Slovak player would actually give.
